children: Gold has rebounded from around $4K after consolidating at that level in June/July, with global liquidity and rising demand potentially supporting a move to $5K or higher, according to Jurrien Timmer, director of global macro at Fidelity Investments.
The metal was around $4,349 as of Sept. 14, down about 22% from the chart's $5,595 peak, while a global-liquidity model pointed to about $5,067, roughly 16.5% above gold's latest level.

The chart compared gold with a model based on global liquidity. It showed the metal climbing sharply through 2025 and into early 2026 before pulling back toward the $4,000 area and subsequently recovering.

The data also tracked global M2 growth and gold ETF flows alongside gold prices. Global M2 growth had reached a labeled peak of 12.0% in early 2026, while the latest gold ETF flow reading was marked at 18.9 on the chart's scale.

On Friday and for the week, gold futures edged higher, showing surprising resilience even after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 and signaled further tightening by year-end.

title: Gold rebounds from $4K support as Timmer sees $5K in sight
